## 2. What to build

**§8 Chat knows the work** (prototype frames 4, 5)
- **A channel links to at most one thing: a project, a client (company or contact) or a team.** "Link to a project, client or team" in Details; **"Start a conversation for X"** in a project's ⋯ and on a client's hub creates a channel named after X, private with X's people when X is private, public otherwise (CH56). Linking a team offers once "Add the team's 4 people?", never kept in sync (CH57). The toolbar shows the item's live chip; Details shows its state; capture from the channel files into the linked project.
- **The item shows its conversation:** "Conversation: Acme · 3 new" on the project overview (TV-U16's slot) and on the client's hub (a row Chat adds to the hub's Linked itself, CV-13), and a quiet **"Mentioned in Acme · Oct 12"** line in any item's Linked when a message mentions it (one line per conversation; only readers of that conversation see it). No "Discuss in chat" button on items.

**§12 Channels: lifecycle and who may do what** (prototype frames 3, 4, 7)
- **New conversation** picks people (a direct message) or makes a channel: name, topic, private or public, people, the announcement switch, an optional link. **Browse channels** lists public channels with Join, and Archived (read only).

**Edge cases this block handles** (§Edge cases)
- Linking a team → "Add the team's 4 people?" once; later team changes don't follow.
- "Start a conversation for X" when X is private → a private channel with exactly the people who can see X; when X is public → a public channel; a name clash → "Acme 2".
- The linked project is archived or deleted → the channel stays; the header chip becomes RF-1's tombstone; capture from it falls back to the Inbox.

## 3. Acceptance criteria

**AC9 — Chat knows the work**
- **AC9.1** a channel links to one project, client or team from Details and from "Start a conversation for X"
- **AC9.2** linking a team offers its people once

**AC5 — A PM's week**
- **AC5.1** "Start a conversation for Website" from the project's ⋯ makes a linked channel; the project overview shows "Conversation: Website · 3 new" (through TV-U16's slot once it lands)

**AC6 — An agency's week (internal chat)**
- **AC6.1** a channel per client linked to the company shows on the client's hub

**Tests that prove them** (file · name · AC · plain English)

- `supabase/tests/chat_links.test.sql` · "linked channels and Mentioned in" · proves AC9.1–9.3, AC5.1, AC6.1, AC3.6 · One link per channel; "Start a conversation for X" picks public or private by X's visibility and names it; a team link adds people once; one "Mentioned in" row per conversation and item, readable by the conversation's readers.

`chat_links.test.sql` is shared with CV-10; this block adds the link half (one link per channel, public/private by `spine__visible_to`, the name and " 2" clash rule, the team offer).

## 4. Decisions that bind it

- **The link** (round-3 §2.21, #6): `chat_channels.linked_type` (`bucket`, `company`, `contact`, `team`) and `linked_id` (both set or both null; `CHAT_LINK_TARGETS` in `@contracts` + a CHECK; index `(linked_type, linked_id) where linked_id is not null`). `chat_op_link_channel(channel, type, id | null)` links or unlinks; the caller must see the item; one link per channel; any poster (§12). It mirrors an `entity_links` row (source the conversation, target the item, relation `conversation-of`, origin `manual`) so the item's Linked, the overview and the client's hub find it through the spine; a team has no registry row, so a team link is the column only. Activity `chat.channel_link` (#15). **`conversation-of` joins `RELATION_KINDS`** (`vocabularies.ts`; `vocabularies.test.ts` and `boundary.test.ts` follow, since the MCP tool args take the list) and the `entity_links` CHECK, re-stated from its live list in the same migration.
- **"Start a conversation for X"** (CH56): `chat_op_create_channel` (**live body**, CV-2b) gains `link_type` / `link_id`; the channel is named after X (" 2", " 3" on a clash); if every workspace member who can use chat can see X it is public with the creator in it, otherwise private with exactly the members who can see X (`spine__visible_to`). From a project's ⋯ (Tasks, `src/features/tasks/ui/`) and from a client's hub (`src/features/contacts/ui/company-hub.tsx`, `contact-hub.tsx`).
- **Linking a team** (CH57): the app offers "Add the team's 4 people?" once and calls `chat_op_add_members`; nothing stays in sync.
- **`chat_conversations_for_item(type, id)`, link half** (CV-10 wrote the mentions half): the linked conversation with the caller's unread count, for "Conversation: Acme · 3 new". Where it shows: the project overview through `ProjectPanel`'s `chat` prop (`ProjectChatSlots`, `src/features/tasks/ui/project-panel.tsx`; **TV-U16 is landed**, so the spec's "until TV-U16 lands" fallback no longer applies); on the client hub **Chat adds the row itself**: the 🟠 box says the hub takes the same `chat` prop, but `company-hub.tsx`, `contact-hub.tsx` and `linked-sections.tsx` have no such prop today: verify, and if absent add the row in the hub's Linked section (`MODULE_SECTIONS` in `linked-sections.tsx`).
- **Toolbar and capture:** the header shows the item's live chip (RF-1 `Reference`; RF-1's tombstone when it is archived or deleted: the channel stays, its "Conversation:" line stays marked archived); Details' "Link to…" (CV-8b's frame) calls the op; capture from a linked channel files into the linked project when the caller can edit it, else the Inbox (CV-10's destination default).

## 7. Watch out

- Round-3 §5 risk 11: the `conversation-of` row must be readable only by people who can read the conversation (CV-1's rule); test as outsider, plain member and key.
- **Tier 2** (migrations, RLS, contracts, moduo-mcp, src/lib/runtime*): one `/code-review high` and one security scan of the diff at the end; scan findings go only into the hand-back.
- **Migration:** stamp provisional (re-cut on apply day, chat's order kept); redefine from live bodies (`pg_get_functiondef`); re-state grants by name (`DROP` + `CREATE` resets them); re-assert the Realtime publication if you publish a table; apply only on your migration turn, then `bun run db:test chat`; never `local:reset` or `migration up` (runbook, `docs/gotchas/supabase.md`).
- **Hot files:** `src/features/chat/store/*` and `src/lib/runtime.chat.web.ts`. Keep edits there small; another builder may change them too.
- **Public repo:** describe no security weakness in any file; tell the orchestrator in the hand-back.

## 8. Out of scope for this block

Decisions on the overview and hub (CV-14, which fills `ProjectChatSlots.decisions`); "Mentioned in" lines (CV-10); the agent tools (CV-21).
